question: The Indian Nationalist leader who delivered lecture on Joseph Mazzini and the ‘Young Italy’ movement was
solution:
The correct answer is __**Surendranath Banerjee.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sir Surendranath Banerjee often known as Rashtraguru was an Indian nationalist leader during British Rule.
 
• The writings of Italian nationalist **Giuseppe Mazzini** influenced **Surendranath**.
 
• He studied the writings of **Mazzini **in his stay in England (1874–1875) on Anandmohan's suggestion.
 
• He founded a nationalist organization called the Indian National Association and was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Surendranath supported Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms, unlike Congress, and with many liberal leaders he left Congress and founded a new organization named Indian National Liberation Federation in 1919.
 
• Surendranath Banerjee was born in Calcutta, in the province of Bengal to a Rarhi Kulin Brahmin family, suggesting that the ancestral seat of the family was in the Rarh region of present-day West Bengal.
 
• In 1879, he bought the newspaper, The Bengalee(founded in 1862 by Girish Chandra Ghosh) and edited it for 40 years in b, when Banerjee was arrested for publishing remarks in his paper.
 
• A Nation in the Making written in the last years of Sir Surendranath Banerjea's life, is not only the autobiography of a pioneering leader in Indian politics but also a commentary on public life.
 
• This book is originally published in 1925.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The young Italy Movement leads by two revolutionaries. One was 'Mazzini' and the other was 'Garibaldi'.
 
• Mazzini
 
 
• To further spread the revolutionary ideas, he founded two more underground societies-* ‘*Young Italy’ in Marseilles and ‘Young Europe’* *in Berne, whose members were like-minded young men from Poland, France, Italy and the German states.
 
• He wanted unification through a democratic revolution but his lofty ideals were not supported by the peasants and middle classes. As a result, he failed in his efforts but prepared the ground for others.
 
• Mazzini believed that God had created nations to be the natural units of mankind. Thus, Italy cannot remain divided into various kingdoms. It has to be a single unified republic.
 
• In 1848, revolts were breaking out all over North Italy. Mazzini took advantage of the circumstances. So, he came to Rome and drove out the Pope. And established Republic in Rome.
 
• Then he formed a committee of three- Triumvirs. Mazzini was one of these Triumvirs. But this young Republic was attacked on all sides: by the Austrians, Neapolitans and the French.
 
 
 
• Garibaldi
 
 
• He was a member of the Young Italy movement. He was skilled in guerrilla warfare and deserves credit for uniting Southern Italian states under the leadership of Piedmont.
 
• He organized a revolutionary force called Red Shirts and succeeded in liberating Sicily and Naples and uniting them under the control of the King of Sardinia.
 
• He was the chief fighter on the side of the Roman Republic. He held the Austrians and defeated the Neapolitan armies. He even stopped the French. All this was done with the help of volunteers
 
• Garibaldi’s leadership gave strength to the young volunteers. Volunteers poured in and they marched enthusiastically. They often marched singing Garibaldi’s hymn.
